finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker could provide a crafted 'country' or 'year' input that alters the constructed URL to point to a malicious server.
finding.assumptions: The URL construction directly uses user input without validation or sanitization.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked whether the constructed URL is passed to any operating‑system command or function that invokes a shell (e.g., system(), popen(), execlp()). The code only passes the URL string to libcurl via curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_URL, url.c_str()), which internally performs an HTTP(S) request using its own networking stack. No shell or OS command is invoked. Therefore the premise of OS command injection is invalid for this code path.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker could provide a crafted 'country' or 'year' input that alters the constructed URL to point to a malicious server.
finding.assumptions: The URL construction directly uses user input without validation or sanitization.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the only operation performed with the constructed URL is setting the CURLOPT_URL option in libcurl; this does not invoke any local command execution or system call. No 'system', 'exec', 'popen', or similar functions are used with the URL string. Therefore the data from the untrusted source cannot reach a command execution sink, invalidating the OS Command Injection claim.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker could provide a crafted webpage that includes malicious content in the 'date' or 'holiday' fields.
finding.assumptions: The XML content is directly used without validation or sanitization.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the reported sink is xmlNodeGetContent, which only returns the textual content of an XML node and does not execute or pass the content to any OS command invocation. No system(), exec(), popen(), or similar call is present in the code. Therefore, the alleged OS Command Injection cannot occur.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker could provide a crafted webpage that includes malicious content in the HTML response.
finding.assumptions: The HTML response is directly parsed without validation or sanitization.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the sink function htmlReadDoc (line 49) and verified that it is a libxml2 parser that merely builds an in-memory DOM from the supplied HTML string. No call to system(), exec*, or similar OS command‑invoking APIs appears in the visible code. The untrusted source "response" is passed only to this parser. Since there is no code path that feeds that parsed content into an OS command, the CWE‑78 claim cannot be satisfied. No additional checks or sanitization are needed for an OS command injection vulnerability.
